title: I Took the Comedy-Club Waitlist to the Door Who Sat Their Friends

parts.text: I took number 8 at 7:41 p.m. and door lead Mace sat three friends from a list that was not the tablet. The stand said: TABLET ONLY. ONE LIST. NO DOOR FRIENDS. I was twenty-six, ticket holder, holding a number. Mace shrugged. "Doors are the room." I photographed the stand, the number, and the friends in my row. Then I asked for the wait log. At 7:47 the manager pinged why Mace's name was on a door list. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see Mace's friends in row seats during my waitlist number.

social.video_title: The door sat three friends off a paper list — Part 1/2
social.description: Comedy club, tablet waitlist, friends in my row. I logged the paper list. Would you have asked the manager?

parts.text: Mace called it energy until the manager asked for the still. I printed the log, the stand, and the number. The friends took the tablet. Mace ran one list and told the next door energy was always about optics. Optics is a word doors use when tablets exist. Waitlist now has a second line: FRIENDS ARE NOT THE ROOM. I keep number 8. Mace brown-bags the jokes. The club finally looks like a tablet, not a living room. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Wait log, tablet list, and a second line. Was energy ever my number?
